hypotheses.title: Active-deformation localisation ridges from the official geodetic strain and seismicity bands
hypotheses.layers: data/raw/training_features.tif band 4 (geodetic second invariant of strain rate), band 7 (geodetic shear rate), band 8 (geodetic dilatation rate), band 16 (earthquake intensity/density), band 10 (distance to earthquake)
hypotheses.physical_signature: not the amplitude but the anisotropic LOCALISATION: multi-scale vesselness / Sato ridge filter plus structure-tensor coherence (|l1|-|l2|)^2/(|l1|+|l2|)^2 at 300-900 m, applied to log(second invariant) and to shear rate, keeping only pixels above the 95th percentile of coherence. Measured here: the raw fields are diffuse - a multi-orientation line operator separates their top 2% from background at only p90 0.0022 vs 0.0008 - so the ridge transform IS the hypothesis, not a refinement.
hypotheses.why_it_catches_a_missing_fault: geodetic strain and microseismicity localise on faults that are currently slipping. A fault can be slipping and be entirely buried under basin alluvium - no scarp, no lineament, no geomorphic expression - and therefore absent from the USGS state-map compilation and from the INGENIOUS Quaternary trace inventory, both of which are mapped from surface geology. Active deformation is the only signal in the official stack that does not require surface expression.
hypotheses.measured_evidence_it_is_unused: lift of C's 37,654 dots over the >200 m moat background by band: second invariant 1.05, shear rate 1.03, dilatation rate 1.06, earthquake intensity 1.04, distance-to-earthquake 1.44 (inverted - C's dots sit FARTHER from earthquakes). Compare TMI horizontal gradient 1.26 and detrended-elevation slope 1.16, which the family does use. Only 0.7-1.4% of C's dots lie in the top 1% of these four bands.
hypotheses.difference_from_repository: H48-3 proposed OPERA InSAR DISP-S1 displacement gradients and was never run ('Earthdata Login required; no granules downloaded'). These bands are already inside the official competition raster, restored byte-identical this session. No file in evidence/ scores a strain-rate or seismicity surface in any form.
hypotheses.data_source: official competition feature raster, restored from five hash-pinned shards at buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE @ c0c06ac82178f26b94fce3397036ef8f12a2f3a0; assembled SHA-256 4371c82e3b8339b807bdffcf4ef59a225520fe2988d521be208ae33743123bc5, 418,912,844 bytes, matching registry/data_manifest_gemsdoe32.json
hypotheses.data_obtainable_how: python scripts/restore_h53_inputs.py --with-official-features  (free, no login, GitHub egress only; 419 MB, deliberately not committed)
hypotheses.expected_dti: unknown but the largest available from data already in hand - the only candidate that could raise the DENSE ceiling above 6,813 rather than re-thinning below it
hypotheses.cost: low-medium: one ridge-filter module, then the existing greedy coverage emitter and pre-registered budget rule; no new downloads
hypotheses.kill_criterion_preregistered: emit the dense ridge field and invert its T under the calibrated |G|. If dense T < 6,813 the field is worse than the backbone and the hypothesis is dead regardless of how good its ridges look. One weekly slot; it also re-calibrates rho for a second family.

hypotheses.title: 3 m lidar scarp TRACES (re-test of H52 with the corrected gate)
hypotheses.layers: data/external/h52_scarp3m_100m.tif bands h_gate12, h_all, sigma_mean, strike_at, cover; upstream USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM, 706 of 716 zone-11 tiles, block-averaged to 3 m then to 100 m in GitHub Actions
hypotheses.physical_signature: line-persistent step height selected as TRACES not points: gate h_gate12 at or above its 99th percentile INSIDE low sigma_mean (smooth terrain, so a step is not merely roughness), then require persistence along a consistent azimuth over >= 5 consecutive 100 m cells, and emit one dot per ~300 m of trace. H52 emitted the top 2,000 individual detections; a fault is a line and the kernel is isotropic, so trace-level selection is a different estimator.
hypotheses.why_it_catches_a_missing_fault: a 100 m DEM cannot resolve a 1-3 m Quaternary scarp at all - the relief is inside one pixel's noise. Every 100 m layer the family uses (detrended elevation, its slope, magnetic gradients) is blind to exactly the young, alluvium-mantled basin faults that a 1 m / 3 m DEM resolves. That is the population an expert reviewer would add to a catalogue.
hypotheses.difference_from_repository: H52 (this repository, 2026-10-07) shipped C + 2,000 point detections and was rejected by two screens this session shows to be unsound: catalogue lift 1.19-2.27x against a >= 2x rule, and 'does not beat H49 on the SGMC proxy'. The re-test changes both the estimator (traces, not points) and the judge (live-calibrated cross-family recalibration, not catalogue lift).
hypotheses.data_source: already committed: data/external/h52_scarp3m_100m.tif (43.8 MB) with data/external/h52_scarp3m_100m.json recording 697 merged tiles and per-tile SHA-256; upstream USGS 3D Elevation Program, https://www.usgs.gov/3d-elevation-program/about-3dep-products-services
hypotheses.blocked_on: units verification. strike_at is quantised to 15-degree bins (observed values 0, 1500, ..., 16500 = 0-165 degrees in 0.01-degree units) and facing_at's units are UNCONFIRMED: the measured median perpendicularity between the two is 46 degrees, not the ~0 degrees a dip-direction/strike pair requires. No along-strike walk may be built on facing_at until src/gemsdoe48/scarp3m.py and data/external/h52_scarp3m_merge_log.txt are re-read against the Actions run that produced them.
hypotheses.expected_dti: highest ceiling of any candidate here - the ceiling analysis shows #1 at 0.3774 needs more truth than the entire backbone contains, and native-resolution lidar is the only data in hand that can supply it
hypotheses.cost: medium: the trace-persistence filter is new code; emitter and budget rule are reused

hypotheses.title: Buried basement steps and isostatic-gravity gradients
hypotheses.layers: official band 15 (depth to basement surface), band 13 (isostatic gravity anomaly), bands 5/11/18 (its slope and vertical/horizontal gradients), band 17 (conductivity surface), band 6 (see irregularity IR-H53-01)
hypotheses.physical_signature: lateral second derivative of basement depth, plus horizontal-gradient magnitude and tilt angle of the isostatic gravity field, intersected with a conductivity contrast (fault gouge and hydrothermal alteration are conductive relative to unaltered basement). Basin-range normal faulting produces a sharp basement-depth step; where the range front is buried the topography is flat but gravity and basement depth still record the offset.
hypotheses.why_it_catches_a_missing_fault: measured blind spot: C's dots sit on SHALLOW basement (mean 402 m against 535 m for the moat background, lift 0.75) and on topographic HIGHS (detrended elevation +7.3 against -15.6). The family therefore systematically favours exposed range fronts. Buried basin-margin faults - a basement step with no topographic expression, in the basin fill - are precisely the population it cannot see, and precisely the population that hosts geothermal reservoirs.
hypotheses.difference_from_repository: H48-2 proposed 'stratigraphic contact topology plus magnetic/gravity breaks' and was never implemented ('payload/coverage not audited'). No file in evidence/ scores a gravity-gradient, basement-depth or conductivity surface.
hypotheses.data_source: same official competition raster as H53-B; same restore command; same pin 4371c82e3b8339b807bdffcf4ef59a225520fe2988d521be208ae33743123bc5
hypotheses.cost: low: data in hand, transforms standard

hypotheses.title: Hydrothermal conduit anchors from GDR well and spring temperature and chemistry
hypotheses.layers: data/raw/external/gdr_wellspring_in_footprint.csv - GDR 1391 'Well and Spring Temperature and Chemistry', 27,092 records; columns used: thermalclass, temp_c, geothermquartz_c, geothermchalc_c, geothermcat_c, row, col, layer, name. dist_known_fault_px is DROPPED ON READ (label-derived leakage).
hypotheses.physical_signature: direct measurement of deep fluid temperature at a point, tiered. Tier 3 = discharge class Hot (median 75.0 C, p90 171.1 C, max 296.5 C) OR any silica/calcite geothermometer >= 150 C (180 records, max 269.1 C). Tier 2 = discharge >= 50 C OR geothermometer >= 100 C. Tier 1 = discharge >= 35 C. Warm (max 38.9 C, effectively ambient) and Cold (<= 20 C) are excluded as non-indicators. No smoothing: a geothermometer is already an integral along the flow path, so the point IS the evidence.
hypotheses.why_it_catches_a_missing_fault: a hot spring needs a heat source, deep circulation and a permeable upflow path; in the extensional Great Basin that path is a fault. Upflow through an already-mapped, already-eroded range front is not what produces a thermal spring in a basin floor - those appear where a BURIED fault carries hot fluid up through alluvium. Measured: of 12,570 distinct grid cells holding a well or spring, 219 (1.7%) lie inside the h19-5 backbone and 11,651 (92.7%) are > 200 m from the public catalogue.
hypotheses.difference_from_repository: H50-GDR used the INGENIOUS 2 m SOIL-temperature probe archive with a repeat-visit residual persistence operator (proxy 0.003923, failed). H52 used lidar topography. H50-B used gamma-ray spectrometry ratios. This uses well/spring DISCHARGE temperature and silica/calcite RESERVOIR geothermometry - a different physical quantity, a different source file, a static tiering operator. No prior GEMSDOE artifact of any session emits on this layer.
hypotheses.data_source: Geothermal Data Registry submission 1391, INGENIOUS Great Basin Regional Dataset Compilation. DOI 10.15121/1881483. https://gdr.openei.org/submissions/1391 . Data.gov metadata https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/ingenious-great-basin-regional-dataset-compilation reports CC BY 4.0; the GDR asset-level attribution/reuse terms were NOT independently verified and are flagged rather than assumed.
hypotheses.expected_dti: 652 anchors shipped; scenario band +0.0019 to +0.0102 live-equivalent as per-anchor credit rises from break-even (0.0556) to 0.30; worst case -0.0019, and A2's in-family gain of +0.0019 pre-pays it (net -0.00003)
hypotheses.cost: low - implemented, tested and shipped this session

hypotheses.title: Three-source Dempster-Shafer conjunction: Quaternary trace x conduit x strain
hypotheses.layers: data/raw/external/gdr_qfaults_traces.csv (1,125 INGENIOUS Quaternary fault trace centroids WITH attributes slip_rate, recency, dip_direct, slip_sense, map_scale, full_length_m, clipped_length_m) x H53-A conduit tier x H53-B strain-rate ridge
hypotheses.physical_signature: CONJUNCTION not union. Extend the frame to three independent sources and admit a dot only where at least two of {a Quaternary trace with a recorded slip rate, a tier >= 2 hydrothermal conduit, a strain-rate localisation ridge} agree within 300 m. slip_rate and recency are used as RELIABILITY WEIGHTS in Dempster's discounting (a trace with slip_rate > 0.2 mm/yr and recency < 1,600,000 yr gets a higher alpha than an unspecified one) - the first use of the attribute columns rather than the geometry alone.
hypotheses.why_it_catches_a_missing_fault: the INGENIOUS Quaternary traces are not the competition catalogue: measured catalogue coverage per pixel 0.3696, the highest of any layer tested, yet only 1.3% of the centroids fall inside the h19-5 backbone. The dropped-catalogue-lift screen says high catalogue coverage is not a reason to trust a layer on its own; the CONJUNCTION is the point. A trace with a measured slip rate AND hot fluid at the surface AND localised active strain is a fault an expert reviewer would add, and each pair alone is much weaker.
hypotheses.difference_from_repository: gemsdoe29-xfit-h41-union-qfaults was a plain UNION and was never live-scored. No prior artifact in any GEMSDOE session used the slip_rate / recency / slip_sense attributes, and none combined THREE sources under Dempster's rule - every fusion in this repository has combined exactly two.
hypotheses.data_source: all three inputs already local and hash-pinned: gdr_qfaults_traces.csv SHA-256 9702f2e5c382a4f472ae834d22b94990983b059677a37adfafd51c50f75e643c, plus the conduit CSV and the official raster
hypotheses.expected_dti: small mass (~100-400 dots), so small in both directions: worst case about -0.001, upside about +0.003 if the conjunction is real
hypotheses.cost: low. Best used as a rider on H53-A once A's live score is known, because A's returned score is what tells us whether conduit evidence carries credit at all.

rejected.idea: Coverage-optimal re-emission of the backbone (greedy max-coverage from scratch)
rejected.why_rejected: Already measured. The frontier maximum is n = 37,167 at model DTI 0.27932, live-equivalent 0.28435. That is the entire in-family prize: +0.00655, only 1.3x the instrument's +/-0.0049 resolution. It also requires REMOVING C dots, forfeiting the only live-verified T in the repository. Not worth a slot on its own.

Already measured, negative, and now reproducible via scripts/compare_coverage_weightings.py -> evidence/coverage_weighting_comparison_20261007.json. Nine target weightings fitted against the eight live scores: uniform RMS 1.758%; far_from_catalogue 1.659% and lidar3m roughness corroboration 1.686% (both within 0.1 percentage points, i.e. noise on eight points, and both specified post hoc); radiometric ratio corroboration 1.796%; log1p density 2.127%; sqrt density 2.305%; density 2.501-2.634%. A corridor pixel is not more likely to sit near hidden truth because it has more corridor neighbours.

rejected.idea: Any re-weighting or fusion of the dotted and tip families (Dempster, Yager, plausibility budget, graded belief, arithmetic mean, alpha=0.99 normalisation)
rejected.why_rejected: Proven impossible to help. Cov(C union h33d) = 79,153.0 at S = 47,905, priced at 0.25879 model / 0.26382 live-equivalent, i.e. -0.01398 against C. The two parents' T differ by 1% (5,209.5 vs 5,157.4) and their Cov by 0.3%, so no combination rule can produce more coverage than the union, and the union's coverage does not pay for its mass. The metric is binary-optimal, so a re-weighting cannot beat its own binarisation.

H50-GDR already ran a repeat-persistence operator on them: proxy 0.003923, 0/4 folds. A different operator is conceivable but the layer is shallow-soil, not deep-fluid, and H53-A's well/spring chemistry is the stronger version of the same idea.

irregularities.title: Two different hidden-truth calibrations coexist in the repository: |G| = 12,632 and |G| = 14,027.5
irregularities.evidence: knowledge/research_notes.md, src/gemsdoe48/holdout.py (HIDDEN_TRUTH_PX = 12632), src/gemsdoe48/live_anchor.py and scripts/build_site_ds48.py all use 12,632, derived by assuming the removed dots earned exactly the tau = 0.05416 bar. This session's least-squares fit over the strictly nested triple A/B/C, assuming the removed dots earned zero, gives 14,027.5 with the three rungs inverting to T = 5,210.4 / 5,216.1 / 5,209.5 - self-consistent to 0.11%. irregularities.action_taken: Both are recorded. 14,027.5 is used everywhere in H53 because it is the value that makes the three nested rungs mutually consistent; the 12,632 assumption is documented as the alternative and its derivation is stated. sources.name: Dempster (1967) and Shafer (1976)
sources.what_it_supports: Dempster's rule of combination and the frame of discernment used for the Bel / Pl / m(Theta) / K layers. Shafer, 'A Mathematical Theory of Evidence', Princeton University Press, 1976.
sources.limit: the rule's normalisation is exactly what produces Zadeh's (1984) paradox; Sentz & Ferson (2002), Sandia SAND2002-0835, document the alternatives. Both K and m(Theta) are therefore shipped rather than one being presented as 'the' disagreement.
